title: Late-afternoon prospect rotations - Nadia
content:
Late-afternoon prospect rotations - quick scratchpad (Nadia)

Goal for session (45–60m): clear 6–8 meaningful next steps, move 3+ accounts into demo/next-call, triage 4 stale leads for either re-qual or archive.

Top priorities right now:
- Finish follow-ups to the 10:30 outbound batch (3 replies waiting)
- Book demos with two mid-market ops leads (Acme Logistics, BrightWave)
- Revisit renewal thread from AtlasHealth — reconcile pricing ask vs. reserved-cap pricing doc (see notes)

Timeblocks
- 14:45–15:15: quick recon + 2 warm callbacks (Acme, BioPulse)
- 15:20–16:00: cold rotations (10 dials + 5 voicemails)
- 16:00–16:30: email blasts / templates / logging
- 16:30–17:15: outreach deep-dive — prioritize follow-ups with context & next-step asks

Call list (ordered by priority)
1) Acme Logistics — Samir Patel (Head of ML Ops) — warm inbound from webinar. Note: interested in dedicated capacity and on-prem eval. Action: send pricing + proposed SOW template. Script: "Samir — quick note with next steps; can we lock 30m next Wed? Have capacity example and latency benchmarks ready."
2) BrightWave Media — Claire Huang (CTO) — demo requested. Action: propose Wed 11am or Thu 3pm, ask about sample prompt set (privacy)
3) AtlasHealth — Priya Rao (Procurement) — pricing pushback. Action: prepare counter-proposal: 6-month reserved + pilot credits. Attach cost-breakdown sheet.
4) BioPulse — Jordan Kim (Director Eng) — follow-up from cold outreach, liked quantization notes. Action: send 1-pager on Redwood Optimize and suggested batching config.
5) Nebula Retail — MQL from Ad, no reply to first email. Action: call then VM: short value prop, request email confirmation to send case study.

Warm follow-ups (quick bullets to send in email or say on call)
- Thanks for taking the time earlier — attaching the two files we discussed (SLA + sample latency report). Next step: 30m demo? Two options: Tue 10am / Thu 2pm.
- For pricing concerns: here is an alternative commit structure (3mo ramp) and a one-page list of observability features included in Dedicated.

Email snippets (use placeholders)
- Quick demo propose:
"Hi {{first_name}}, thanks again for the convo — can we lock 30m to walk through a short demo and the deployment options? I can do {{option_1}} or {{option_2}}. If you'd like, I can run the demo against a tiny sample of your prompts to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
Best, Nadia"

- Pricing reply:
"Hi {{first_name}}, I hear you on predictable costs. Two options below: 1) Reserved capacity (monthly commit) with burst buffer; 2) Hosted + predictable throughput plan with cost caps for X months. Attached: quick cost comparison PDF and recommended configuration for your traffic profile."

Objection playbook (short counters)
- "Too expensive" -> show unit economics: cost/token vs. latency tradeoff, offer trial/commit to prove ROI.
- "We host everything" -> highlight private deploy + on-prem integration + KMS support. Offer architecture review with Infra.
- "Need compliance" -> call out audit logs, SOC2 and enterprise package, propose convo with Security PM.

Logging / dispositions (what to mark in CRM)
- Interested-demo (booked)
- Needs-pricing (send counter + follow-up in 3 days)
- Not-now (Nurture: 90-day cadence)
- Not-a-fit (close and archive)

Notes to self / micro-tasks
- Attach the reserved-cap pricing sheet (v2) from /sales/templates — tweak commit numbers for Acme
- Ping Marco for AtlasHealth pricing approval (ticket JIRA-PL-4021)
- Add BrightWave to demo running order and prep example prompts (media ad copy, 512 tokens)
- Create one new subject line variant for cold reach: "Reduce LLM inference cost by 30% without accuracy loss" (A/B test)

Unresolved questions
- Does AtlasHealth require HSM for key management (ask Security)
- BrightWave: do they want streaming or batch generation? (ask Claire in discovery)

Quick reference links
- Pricing matrix (internal): confluence.sales/pricing-matrix-2026
- Demo checklist: github.com/redwood/demo-checklist (private)

End-of-session goals (tick when done)
[ ] Book 2 demos
[ ] Get pricing decision on AtlasHealth
[ ] Clear 6 follow-ups and log CRM notes

Random scratch / talking points (toss into call if there's silence)
- "We run a lot of workloads where prefix caching cuts token costs by ~25% for typical sequences — happy to show an example with your prompts."
- "If latency is a hard constraint, we can pin to a lower-capacity model variant and fallback policy to preserve availability."

Tiny personal reminder
- Bring lunch tomorrow; 12:30 buddy check with Marco.

-- End of pad --

(Will copy snippets into CRM and update JIRA after session)
